from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Constraints ensure unique PDE solutions.",
            "Initial conditions set state at time zero.",
            "Boundaries fix edges, like a guitar string."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Boundary and Initial Conditions", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Representing Dirichlet condition: u = 0 at boundaries
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[-1, 1, 1], axis_config={"include_numbers": False}).scale(0.5)
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(np.pi * x / 4), color=BLUE)
        dots = VGroup(Dot(axes.c2p(0, 0), color=RED), Dot(axes.c2p(4, 0), color=RED))
        group = VGroup(axes, curve, dots)
        self.place_in_area(group, 'B2', 'D5', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(group))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Initial condition u(x,0) pulse
        pulse = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.8 * np.exp(-(x-2)**2), color=GREEN)
        self.play(Transform(curve, pulse))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREEN)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Guitar string metaphor (vibrating motion)
        self.play(Indicate(dots))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(RED)
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Applications and Summary", [
            "PDEs model complex real-world phenomena.",
            "From weather patterns to financial markets.",
            "Modeling, constraints, and solving define PDEs."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        heat_map = Square(side_length=2, fill_opacity=0.6, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_in_area(heat_map, 'B2', 'D4', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(Create(heat_map))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREEN)
        weather_icon = Dot(radius=0.5, color=BLUE_B)
        self.place_at_grid(weather_icon, 'C5', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(weather_icon))
        self.play(weather_icon.animate.shift(RIGHT * 0.5))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(ORANGE)
        checklist = VGroup(
            Text("1. Model", font_size=20),
            Text("2. Constraints", font_size=20),
            Text("3. Solve", font_size=20)
        ).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT)
        self.place_in_area(checklist, 'D2', 'F4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(checklist))
        self.wait(2)

sections.title: From ODEs to PDEs: A Visual Shift
sections.content: Recall Ordinary Differential Equations (ODEs) where a function depends on one variable. Introduce PDEs as the language of multi-variable change. Use an animation showing a point moving along a line (ODE) versus a surface ripple (PDE).
sections.example: A cat walking on a 1D path vs. a drop of water creating circular ripples on a 2D pond surface.

sections.title: Defining the Operators
sections.content: Introduce partial derivatives (∂/∂x, ∂/∂t) as 'looking' at change from specific directions. Use a 3D hill visualization where the slope is color-coded to show gradient changes along the X and Y axes independently.
sections.example: A hiker measuring the steepness of a mountain slope facing North vs. the steepness facing East.

sections.title: The Heat Equation: A Core PDE
sections.content: Present the Heat Equation (ut = αuxx). Explain it as: 'the rate of change of temperature over time is proportional to the curvature of temperature in space.' Use a heatmap animation showing a hot iron rod cooling down.
sections.example: An animation of a glowing-hot metal bar turning blue as it loses heat to the room, showing heat 'smoothing out' over time.

sections.title: Boundary and Initial Conditions
sections.content: Explain that PDEs need 'rules' to have a unique solution. Introduce Initial Conditions (the state at t=0) and Boundary Conditions (what happens at the edges). Use an animation of a vibrating guitar string held at both ends.
sections.example: A guitar string: the 'Initial Condition' is the shape of the pluck; the 'Boundary Conditions' are the fixed ends at the nut and bridge.

sections.title: Applications and Summary
sections.content: Conclude by showcasing the ubiquity of PDEs in real life, from fluid dynamics to finance. Summarize the workflow: Model (PDE) -> Add Constraints (Boundaries) -> Solve.
sections.example: A weather satellite map demonstrating how PDEs predict the movement of a hurricane by calculating pressure and wind velocity fields.
